summary: Extend the existing audit capability with its registered PostgreSQL infrastructure adapter and production-grade append-only persistence controls.

impacts.evidence: The PostgreSQL adapter binds transaction-local organization and workspace scope, while split audit RLS policies independently enforce tenant reads and inserts.
Audit summaries are bounded and recursively sanitized before persistence so credentials and raw authorization material do not become durable audit data.
Task 003 adds no public REST endpoint or OpenAPI operation and therefore does not change the existing external API compatibility surface.
The implementation persists application audit records directly and introduces no Kafka event family, envelope change, or public event-version transition.
The audit service and PostgreSQL adapter remain internal platform capabilities and do not modify connector or plugin SDK contracts or provider admission.
Immutable migration 000004 adds the audit risk column, bounded summary constraints, split RLS policies, append-only triggers, and atomic migration-history recording.
Application and database layers both reject unsafe audit content, while database triggers block update, delete, and truncate attempts even outside normal RLS paths.
Every new application audit event carries one canonical operation risk class, preserving an explicit risk signal for later approval and governance capabilities.
The task establishes immutable actor, source, action, resource, correlation, risk, summary, tenant, identifier, and timestamp lineage for application effects.
Audit capture adds a persistence side effect but does not define reconciliation state, inbox deduplication, retry ownership, or idempotency semantics for business operations.
The audit foundation has no webhook delivery or external network egress behavior; it writes only through the internal PostgreSQL persistence boundary.
Task 003 adds no SLO thresholds, metrics contract, tracing backend, or alert-routing change; observability policy remains owned by its existing platform work.
The expand migration preserves legacy nullable actor/correlation fields and a legacy risk default while upgrade and backup rehearsal scripts now apply atomic migrations correctly.
New unit, static migration, schema fixture, RLS smoke, append-only mutation, migration catalog, race, and repeated package tests cover the audit boundary.
